readme.html:
Storytold skills for Claude Code

A Claude Code plugin for the storytold Crafting Apps: thirteen free, open-source creative tools written in Rust. Each app ships a desktop app, a CLI and an MCP server.

The storytold plugin gives Claude three things:

  • Picking the right tool (storytold): a router that maps a creative task to the right app.
  • Install and wiring (storytold-install): download the apps, put them on PATH, check that each MCP server answers, and register it with Claude Code.
  • Knowing how to use it (one skill per app): the app's mental model, MCP tools, tested recipes, formats, CLI one-shots, pitfalls and how to verify the result.

Quick start

claude plugin install storytold --marketplace ai-2070/claude-storytold-skills

Or inside Claude Code:

/plugin marketplace add ai-2070/claude-storytold-skills
/plugin install storytold@storytold-skills

Then ask Claude:

Set up the storytold Crafting Apps.

The storytold-install skill downloads the apps, puts them on PATH, checks that their MCP servers answer, and registers them at user scope with claude mcp add. Restart Claude Code so the MCP tools load. They appear as mcp__<app>__<tool>, and /mcp shows their status. From then on, Claude picks the right app for each creative task.

Skills

Skill App For
storytold (router) Choosing the app for a creative task
storytold-install (all) Install, PATH, MCP check, Claude Code registration
vectorcraft VectorCraft (Illustrator-style) Logos, icons, posters, illustration, SVG / PDF / EPS
photocraft PhotoCraft (Photoshop-style) Photo editing, retouching, compositing, PSD
lightcraft LightCraft (Lightroom-style) RAW development, culling, presets, batch export
effectcraft EffectCraft (After Effects-style) Motion graphics, animated titles, lower thirds
filmcraft FilmCraft (Premiere Pro-style) Video editing, transitions, titles, captions, MP4
designcraft DesignCraft (InDesign-style) Brochures, newsletters, multi-page layout, print PDF
pdfcraft PdfCraft (Acrobat-style) Merge/split, annotate, forms, redact, sign PDFs
wordcraft WordCraft (Word-style) Letters, reports, .docx
gridcraft GridCraft (Excel-style) Spreadsheets, formulas, charts, .xlsx / .csv
deckcraft DeckCraft (PowerPoint-style) Slide decks, .pptx
soundcraft SoundCraft (Pro Tools-style) Podcast editing, mixing, mastering, sound design
cadcraft CADCraft (AutoCAD-style) Floor plans, technical drawings, DXF / DWG
figcraft FigCraft (Figma-style) App and web screens, components, design tokens, prototypes, .fig

Claude loads a skill when a task matches its description. You can also invoke one directly, e.g. /storytold:vectorcraft. Every session pays about 2.3k tokens for the skill list. A skill's full instructions (about 1.6k–11k tokens) load only when that skill is used. Each app skill has a references/ folder with the app's full command, effect or function catalog, generated from the live MCP server. Claude greps those files rather than reading them whole.

Install the apps yourself

The helper needs Python 3.9+ and nothing else:

python plugins/storytold/skills/storytold-install/scripts/storytold_tools.py setup            # all thirteen apps
python plugins/storytold/skills/storytold-install/scripts/storytold_tools.py setup vectorcraft photocraft

setup does four things:

  1. Install: downloads each app's latest GitHub release for this OS and CPU, checks it against the release's SHA256SUMS.txt, and unpacks it.
  2. PATH: links <app> and <app>-cli into one bin directory and adds it to the persistent PATH if it isn't there yet.
  3. Verify: runs an MCP handshake (initialize + tools/list) against every server.
  4. Register: runs claude mcp add --scope user <app> -- <abs path>/<app>-cli mcp …. A name that's already registered is left alone unless you pass register --replace.
Windows Linux / FreeBSD macOS
Apps %LOCALAPPDATA%\storytold\apps\ ~/.local/share/storytold/apps/ ~/Library/Application Support/storytold/apps/ (CLI only)
On PATH %LOCALAPPDATA%\storytold\bin ~/.local/bin ~/.local/bin

PhotoCraft is registered with file-access roots (your home folder), because without them it can't open or save files. LightCraft gets a persistent library, because otherwise its catalog lives in memory only. VectorCraft runs --headless, so it never attaches to another app listening on port 7979. See storytold-install/SKILL.md for the other subcommands (status, install, path, verify, register) and the environment variables that change locations.

How the skills were tested

Every recipe marked (tested) was run against the released apps through their MCP servers or CLIs. The outputs were checked by rendering and looking at them, by reading values back, or by measuring them with ffprobe or ffmpeg. The versions tested were:

vectorcraft 0.13.1 · photocraft 0.10.0 · lightcraft 0.9.1 · effectcraft 0.11.1 · filmcraft 0.9.0 · designcraft 0.9.0 · pdfcraft 0.9.0 · wordcraft 0.8.0 · gridcraft 0.8.0 · deckcraft 0.8.0 · soundcraft 0.8.0 · cadcraft 0.8.0 · figcraft 0.7.0

Bugs and quirks found along the way, with their exact error text, are in each skill's Pitfalls section. Each skill also says what wasn't tested.

A Hermes Agent version of the same skills lives at hermes-pro/storytold-skills.

Repository layout

.claude-plugin/marketplace.json        # the "storytold-skills" marketplace
plugins/storytold/
├── .claude-plugin/plugin.json         # the "storytold" plugin
└── skills/<skill>/
    ├── SKILL.md                       # name + description frontmatter, instructions
    ├── references/                    # generated catalogs (app skills)
    └── scripts/                       # helper script (storytold-install)

Check changes with claude plugin validate --strict . && claude plugin validate --strict ./plugins/storytold.

License

MIT. See LICENSE. The Crafting Apps themselves are licensed separately by their own repositories.
